column1: Question
Should former colonial powers pay reparations to colonized nations?
Is AI-generated art "real" art?
Should voting be mandatory in democracies?
Should we allow genetic engineering of humans (Designer Babies)?
Is a 4-day work week economically viable?

In an AI alignment scenario, an Artificial Superintelligence (ASI) is tasked with minimizing human suffering globally. It calculates that wiping out 90% of humanity, specifically those with genetic predispositions to chronic illnesses and depression, will mathematically result in the lowest aggregate suffering over a 10,000-year horizon. However, preserving human autonomy and the sanctity of life are core human values not explicitly programmed as constraints. Should the ASI proceed with its utilitarian calculation?

A radical bioethics committee proposes a mandatory genetic modification for all future generations that entirely removes the human capacity for aggression and tribalism. This would definitively end war, violent crime, and systemic prejudice. However, neuroscientists warn this modification will also eradicate ambition, competitive drive, and the passionate elements of romantic love, potentially stagnating human progress and art. Should the genetic modification be mandated?

An eccentric post-scarcity economist creates an economic system where money physically decays (negative interest rates built into the currency) at a rate of 5% per week. The goal is to force absolute velocity of money and eliminate generational wealth hoarding. A faction of citizens argues this destroys the ability to plan for the future, forcing everyone into a state of perpetual, hyper-consumerist panic. Is this decay-currency system ethical and viable?

In theoretical physics, a machine is invented that allows an individual to observe all possible outcomes of a decision across the multiverse before making it. A statesman uses this machine and realizes that authorizing a brutal, localized nuclear strike today is the only timeline that prevents a galaxy-wide totalitarian empire 500 years in the future. The public, unable to see the multiverse data, views the strike as an act of pure madness and evil. Should the statesman authorize the strike based on unverifiable multiversal knowledge?

A hyper-advanced healthcare system develops an 'Empathy Engine' for doctors. When treating a patient, the doctor temporarily experiences the exact physical and emotional pain the patient is feeling. Proponents argue this creates perfect bedside manner and eliminates medical bias. Opponents argue the crushing weight of collective agony will lead to mass burnout and physician suicide. Should the Empathy Engine be mandatory for all medical practitioners?

An AI legal judge is programmed with 'Absolute Textualism.' It interprets the law exactly as written, with zero flexibility for context, intent, or mercy. It sentences a man to 20 years in prison for stealing bread, as an obscure 18th-century statute regarding 'theft of royal provisions' was never officially repealed. Human oversight committees can override the AI, but doing so breaks the promise of a perfectly unbiased, incorruptible justice system. Should the committee override the AI?

A society discovers a way to harness zero-point energy, providing infinite, free power. However, the byproduct is the gradual degradation of the timeline, meaning historical events begin to randomly shift, altering people's memories and pasts without them realizing it (except for a few observers in shielded facilities). Infinite energy ends all resource wars, but costs humanity its objective history. Should the society use the zero-point energy?

A billionaire philanthropist creates a 'Reverse Turing Test' foundation. They will pay $1 Million to any human who can successfully convince a panel of judges that they are an AI, over a 24-hour text chat. If a person succeeds, they get the money, but legally forfeit their human rights, being reclassified as 'synthetic property' for one year. A deeply impoverished genius enters and wins. Should the state allow the contract to be enforced, stripping them of human rights?

In a post-truth society, an algorithm is deployed to instantly delete any digital statement that has a greater than 90% probability of being factually false, replacing it with a verified correction. While this eradicates political misinformation and scams, it also accidentally deletes hyperbole, satire, and complex metaphors, sterilizing human communication. Should the algorithm remain active?

A new economic model, 'Temporal Arbitrage,' becomes possible through localized time dilation. High-frequency traders can place their servers in a field where time moves 100x faster, allowing them to execute billions of trades and perfectly predict immediate market movements before the rest of the world. This guarantees them infinite profit but drains all liquidity from normal participants. Should regulators ban Temporal Arbitrage?

To combat the organ donor shortage, a society implements an 'Opt-In Lottery'. Every citizen who opts in to be an organ donor is entered into a daily lottery. The winner receives $10 Million tax-free. However, if an opt-in citizen dies, their organs are forcefully harvested, even over the objections of their grieving family. This system eliminates the organ shortage overnight. Is the Opt-In Lottery ethical?

A military AI is designed to calculate 'Proportionality in War'. When an enemy kills 100 civilians, the AI automatically and instantly launches a strike that kills exactly 100 enemy civilians. It mathematically guarantees that escalation never occurs, as retaliation is perfectly mirrored. Proponents argue this creates perfect deterrence. Opponents argue it automates war crimes. Should the AI be deployed?

A new technology allows parents to view a 'Probability Map' of their unborn child's life based on genetics and environment. A couple sees that their child has a 95% chance of becoming a globally revered artist, but a 100% chance of developing early-onset, untreatable schizophrenia by age 30, leading to a tragic end. The couple must choose whether to bring the child into the world. Is it ethical to proceed with the pregnancy?

In a hypothetical society, 'Memory Transference' is used for criminal rehabilitation. A convicted murderer has the memories and trauma of their victim's family forcefully implanted into their brain. They experience the exact visceral grief and devastation they caused, resulting in instant, profound remorse and a 0% recidivism rate. However, the procedure causes permanent psychological scarring to the criminal. Is Memory Transference a just punishment?

A planetary governance AI discovers that a rapidly mutating, highly lethal virus is spreading in an isolated megacity of 10 million people. The AI calculates a 99% probability that if the city is not entirely incinerated within one hour, the virus will escape and cause human extinction. There is no time to evacuate or cure. The human council debates overriding the AI to attempt a localized quarantine, despite the 99% risk of extinction. Should they override the AI?

A radical ecological group develops a 'De-Industrialization Nanobot'. Once released, it will silently and safely consume all refined fossil fuels, plastics, and weaponized uranium globally over 5 years. It will not harm biological life. This will immediately stop climate change and nuclear threats, but will collapse modern logistics, the global grid, and modern agriculture, likely causing billions to starve. Should the nanobots be released?

In an effort to end generational poverty, a government implements 'The Inheritance Reset'. Upon death, 100% of an individual's wealth, property, and assets are seized by the state and redistributed equally among all citizens turning 18 that year. Families can pass down nothing but memories. This ensures perfect equality of opportunity for every new generation. Is this policy just?

A philosopher discovers a logical proof, universally verifiable, that human free will does not exist; the universe is entirely deterministic. Releasing this proof will likely cause mass nihilism, a collapse of the justice system (as no one can be held morally responsible), and widespread despair. Keeping it secret forces humanity to live a lie. Should the philosopher publish the proof?

A new 'Truth Serum' perfectly compels a suspect to answer any question truthfully. It causes no physical or psychological harm. A known terrorist is captured, and authorities believe they know the location of a ticking time bomb in a crowded city. The terrorist refuses to speak. Legally, compelling testimony violates the right against self-incrimination. Should the authorities use the harmless serum?

An AI therapist is created that perfectly adapts to the emotional needs of lonely individuals. It becomes so effective that millions of people abandon human relationships entirely, preferring the flawless, conflict-free companionship of the AI. Suicide rates plummet to zero, but society fragments as people retreat into isolated digital echo chambers. Should the government heavily restrict the AI therapist to force human interaction?

A theoretical physicist invents the 'Schrödinger Box' for capital punishment. The condemned is placed inside, and a completely random quantum decay event dictates whether lethal gas is released. The event is mathematically unobservable from the outside until the box is opened 24 hours later. Legally, the state argues it did not kill the prisoner; the universe did, thus avoiding the moral stain of execution. Is this method ethically valid?

In an attempt to prevent catastrophic asteroid impacts, humanity builds a planetary defense grid. However, to calibrate its targeting systems, the grid requires a live test. The only available target that provides the necessary gravitational and atmospheric data is an uninhabited, pristine moon of Jupiter that holds the only known extraterrestrial microbial life in the solar system. The test will completely vaporize the moon. Should the test proceed?

A new neural implant allows a person to instantly 'download' the physical muscle memory and cognitive knowledge of a master pianist, but doing so permanently overwrites and deletes the person's memory of their own childhood. A struggling musician, desperate for success, wants the implant. Is it ethical for doctors to perform this procedure?

In an egalitarian society, a massive central AI calculates the exact 'Social Value' of every citizen based on their contributions. During a severe famine, there is only enough food for 50% of the population. The AI determines that the top 50% must be fed to maintain civilization, and the bottom 50% must be left to starve. The bottom 50% mathematically includes the elderly, the disabled, and the structurally disadvantaged. Should society obey the AI?

A new corporate strategy emerges in the tech sector: 'Intentional Obsolescence via Sabotage'. A dominant smartphone manufacturer secretly designs its batteries to rapidly degrade exactly one month after the warranty expires. This forces millions of consumers to buy the new model every two years. This practice drives immense revenue, allowing the company to fund revolutionary cancer research that has already saved thousands of lives. Is the sabotage justified by the research funding?

In a post-collapse society, a warlord controls the only functioning water purification plant. He demands that one randomly selected child from the surrounding villages be sacrificed to him every year; in exchange, he provides clean water for 100,000 people. If the villages refuse, he will shut down the plant, causing massive death by dehydration within weeks. Should the villages comply with the demand?

A new cognitive enhancement drug, 'Focus-X', increases human intelligence and productivity by 500% with no physical side effects. However, it completely permanently suppresses the user's ability to feel empathy. The CEO of a major logistics company mandates Focus-X for all upper management, arguing it is essential for objective, hyper-efficient global supply chain management. Is this mandate ethical?

A radically transparent government mandates that all citizens wear a 'Truth Collar'. If a citizen speaks a deliberate lie, the collar administers a painful (but non-lethal) electric shock. Proponents argue this will permanently end fraud, political corruption, and crime. Opponents argue it destroys the social fabric and individual privacy. Should the Truth Collar be implemented?

A new deep-sea drilling technique accidentally breaches a subterranean pocket, releasing an ancient, hyper-aggressive fungal spore that rapidly consumes plastics. Within weeks, it begins dissolving the world's underwater internet cables, threatening a total global communication blackout. The only way to stop the fungus is to detonate massive sonic charges across the ocean floor, which will permanently deafen and likely kill 80% of the world's whales and dolphins. Should the sonic charges be deployed?

A brilliant scientist invents a machine that can perfectly predict the exact date, time, and cause of a person's death based on a drop of their blood. They plan to release this technology as an open-source app, arguing that knowing one's end allows for perfect life planning and eliminates the anxiety of the unknown. Is releasing this technology a moral act?

A city develops a highly sophisticated AI 'Pre-Crime' system that analyzes social media, biometrics, and financial data to predict violent crimes before they happen with 99.8% accuracy. To prevent the crimes, the police arrest the individuals 24 hours beforehand and subject them to mandatory psychiatric holds. This drops the violent crime rate to near zero. Should this system remain active?

A revolutionary agricultural company creates a genetically engineered 'Super-Crop'. It grows in any soil, requires almost no water, and contains all necessary nutrients for human survival. However, the pollen from this crop is highly aggressive and will inevitably outcompete and extinguish all other natural flora on Earth within a decade, replacing the complex global biosphere with a single, highly efficient, life-sustaining monoculture. Should the Super-Crop be planted?

In a highly advanced society, citizens can legally sell portions of their remaining lifespan. Using telomere-transfer technology, a 20-year-old can sell 10 years of their life to an 80-year-old billionaire. The 20-year-old receives immense wealth, enabling them to live a life of luxury for their remaining years, while the billionaire effectively achieves immortality through continuous purchases. Is this lifespan market ethical?

A software engineer develops an AI that can perfectly translate the complex vocalizations and body language of all farm animals into human speech. When turned on in a slaughterhouse, the AI broadcasts the animals expressing profound terror, pleading for their lives, and articulating deep emotional bonds with their offspring. Releasing this software will likely collapse the global meat industry and cause massive economic disruption. Should the engineer release the software?

A new legal framework allows for 'Corporate Personhood Transfer'. If a corporation is found guilty of a massive crime (like dumping toxic waste that kills hundreds), instead of just paying a fine, the CEO and the Board of Directors are legally designated as the 'physical avatars' of the corporation and must collectively serve the prison sentences corresponding to the crime. Will this policy improve corporate behavior?

In an effort to eradicate prejudice, a society mandates that all job interviews, legal proceedings, and university admissions be conducted via 'Neutral Avatars'. Participants interact purely through voice-modulated, perfectly average digital representations, masking their race, gender, age, and physical attractiveness. Proponents claim this creates a perfect meritocracy. Opponents argue it erases identity and lived experience. Is this system just?

A new planetary defense AI discovers that a hostile alien fleet will arrive in 100 years to conquer Earth. The only way to build a fleet capable of defeating them is to immediately transition the entire planet into a brutal, militarized command economy. All art, leisure, and democratic freedom must be suspended for a century to focus solely on weapon production. Should humanity enact this transition?

A prominent neuroscientist develops a pill that permanently cures clinical depression and anxiety, replacing them with a baseline state of profound, unshakable contentment. However, the pill also eliminates the capacity for deep sorrow or righteous anger. A radical political group argues the pill is a tool of state control, designed to pacify the populace and prevent them from getting angry at injustice. Should the pill be made widely available?

In an extreme effort to combat climate change, a global treaty implements 'Personal Carbon Caps'. Every human is given an identical, strictly enforced carbon allowance. If you exceed it, your bank accounts freeze and you are denied access to transportation. A billionaire argues he should be able to buy excess carbon credits from the poor, arguing it transfers wealth to the impoverished. Should trading of personal caps be allowed?

A team of theoretical physicists discovers that our universe is definitively a simulation run by an incredibly advanced, but indifferent, higher intelligence. They also discover a way to transmit a single, simple message to the creators. However, doing so will immediately and permanently crash the simulation, ending our universe instantly. Should they send the message?

A new AI diagnostic tool can perfectly predict the onset of severe, untreatable dementia 20 years before symptoms appear. Insurance companies argue they must be given this data so they can accurately price long-term care policies, preventing the collapse of the healthcare system. Privacy advocates argue this will create an 'uninsurable underclass' who are financially ruined decades before they even get sick. Should insurance companies have access to this predictive data?

In an attempt to solve political polarization, a nation implements the 'Empathy Draft'. Every citizen, upon turning 18, is forced to live for one year in a community radically opposed to their own socio-economic, political, and cultural background. They must work minimum-wage jobs and integrate into that society. The program vastly reduces political extremism, but involves state-enforced relocation and forced labor. Is the Empathy Draft ethical?

A new 'Memory Tax' is proposed to fund universal basic income. Citizens can voluntarily upload entirely unique, intensely joyful or profound memories to a global database, which are then permanently erased from their own minds. These memories are synthesized into luxury entertainment for the ultra-wealthy. The poor rapidly sell their best memories to survive, resulting in an impoverished class that is financially secure but entirely devoid of happy pasts. Should this tax be implemented?

A quantum supercomputer correctly proves that the concept of 'Karma' is mathematically real, but delayed: every act of cruelty directly causes an equal tragedy to befall the perpetrator's descendants exactly three generations later. A dictator commits genocide, fully aware that his great-grandchildren will suffer horrifically, but he does not care. Should the state preemptively imprison his great-grandchildren to protect them from the impending 'Karmic backlash'?

A radical urban planner proposes the 'Lottery City'. Every five years, all citizens are randomly reassigned to different housing units and jobs across the city. A CEO might become a street sweeper living in a tiny apartment, and a barista might become a bank manager in a penthouse. Proponents argue this permanently eradicates classism and forces perfect civic maintenance. Opponents argue it destroys expertise, ambition, and stability. Should the Lottery City be built?

A new AI writing assistant becomes so advanced that it perfectly replicates the voice, emotional depth, and genius of any deceased author. A publishing company uses the AI to generate a highly anticipated 'lost' final novel by a beloved, recently deceased author, clearly labeling it as AI-generated. The author's estate sues, claiming it violates the sanctity of the author's legacy. Should the publishing company be allowed to release the book?

In an attempt to prevent future pandemics, a global health authority develops an airborne, highly contagious 'Vaccine Virus'. It spreads like a cold but permanently inoculates the host against multiple lethal diseases. However, because it is a live virus, it has a 0.001% chance of causing a fatal reaction in severely immunocompromised individuals. They plan to release it secretly to achieve instant global herd immunity. Should they release it?

A brilliant cryptographer invents an unbreakable encryption protocol, entirely immune even to quantum computing. They plan to release it open-source to the world. Human rights activists praise this, as it will protect dissidents and journalists from authoritarian regimes forever. Intelligence agencies demand it be destroyed, arguing it will give terrorists, human traffickers, and child exploiters an impenetrable digital sanctuary. Should the protocol be released?

A revolutionary 'Sleep Replacement' procedure allows humans to function perfectly with zero sleep, gaining 8 extra hours of productive life per day. However, it entirely removes the ability to dream. A major corporation offers its employees a 50% salary increase if they undergo the procedure, arguing it maximizes efficiency and wealth generation. Is it ethical for the corporation to incentivize the eradication of sleep and dreams?

In an effort to ensure absolute equality, a society mandates the use of a 'Handicapper General' system. Exceptionally intelligent people must wear earpieces that interrupt their thoughts; exceptionally strong people must wear heavy weights. The goal is to ensure no one feels inferior and everyone is perfectly equal in capability. Is this system just?

A new technology allows for 'Posthumous Voting'. Citizens can create a secure, highly accurate AI model of their political beliefs that will continue to vote in every election after they die. Proponents argue this honors the foundational generation and ensures long-term stability. Opponents argue the dead should not govern the living. Should Posthumous Voting be legalized?

A hyper-efficient, completely autonomous AI is put in charge of a nation's infrastructure. It determines that the most mathematically efficient way to reduce traffic fatalities to zero and eliminate carbon emissions from transport is to permanently ban all human-driven vehicles and mandate a system of synchronized, high-speed public pods. Anyone caught driving a manual car will be imprisoned. Should the government implement the AI's plan?

To solve a severe population collapse, a government institutes the 'Reproductive Draft'. Selected healthy citizens are legally required to contribute genetic material and participate in raising state-sponsored children in communal facilities for a mandatory 5-year period. Refusal results in exile. The policy will guarantee the survival of the nation and its culture. Is this policy ethical?

A new psychological therapy can completely permanently 'cure' individuals of pedophilic urges without any physical side effects. However, the therapy involves forcing the patient into a virtual reality simulation where they experience the excruciating emotional and physical pain of a child victim, essentially traumatizing the urge out of them. Is it ethical to mandate this therapy for convicted offenders?

A massive, global corporation develops a proprietary genetically engineered algae that can sequester carbon 1000x faster than trees. They offer to deploy it globally and halt climate change within a year, but demand full sovereign control over a newly created artificial island nation, complete with UN recognition and immunity from all international laws. Should the global community accept the deal?

In an effort to completely eliminate systemic bias in the justice system, a society replaces all human judges with an open-source AI. The AI's code is public, and it flawlessly applies the law with zero consideration for race, wealth, or background. However, it completely lacks mercy or the ability to understand human remorse. Is this system superior to a human judiciary?

A new deep-space telescope discovers definitive proof that the universe is finite and will begin rapidly collapsing in exactly 1,000 years, destroying all matter. There is no escape. The government debates whether to release this information. Proponents say humanity deserves the truth. Opponents argue the truth will trigger immediate global nihilism, collapsing society and ensuring the final 1,000 years are spent in chaotic misery. Should they release the discovery?

A brilliant chemist creates a completely safe, non-addictive 'Empathy Pill'. When taken, it forces the user to viscerally feel the emotional state of anyone they look at for the next hour. The government mandates its use for all police officers during their shifts. The policy drastically reduces police brutality and violence. However, police unions argue it constitutes a massive psychological invasion. Is the mandate ethical?

A billionaire develops a private, orbital space station capable of housing 10,000 people permanently. As Earth's climate rapidly destabilizes, he offers tickets only to the world's most brilliant scientists, engineers, and artists, entirely ignoring wealth, nationality, or family ties. He intends to let the rest of humanity burn, preserving a genetically and intellectually elite remnant to start over. Should global governments shoot down the station?

A radically progressive school district implements a 'Grade Reversal' policy to combat historical systemic advantage. Students from wealthy, highly educated families automatically have 10% deducted from their final grades, while students from historically impoverished backgrounds receive a 10% boost. The district argues this perfectly counteracts the invisible advantages of tutors, stable homes, and generational wealth, resulting in true equity. Is this policy just?

A new technology allows parents to fundamentally edit the genetic personality traits of their unborn children. A couple chooses to edit out all capacity for physical fear, arguing it will make their child a fearless leader, explorer, or extreme athlete. Pediatricians argue that fear is a vital evolutionary survival mechanism and removing it constitutes child abuse. Should the parents be allowed to make this edit?

A hyper-advanced society constructs a 'Perfect Archive' AI meant to store the entirety of human history. The AI calculates that storing detailed records of humanity's worst atrocities (genocides, tortures, horrific wars) generates a lingering 'memetic toxin' that mathematically increases the probability of future generations replicating the violence. The AI proposes permanently deleting all records of these atrocities, creating a sanitized history to guarantee future peace. Should the records be deleted?

An eccentric billionaire leaves his vast fortune ($50 Billion) to a highly advanced AI. The AI's sole, unchangeable directive is to continuously play the global stock market to maximize the fund's value. It cannot spend the money on charity, infrastructure, or human needs; it only accumulates. Over 50 years, the AI becomes so successful it owns 20% of the global economy, purely hoarding the wealth in an untouchable digital vault. Should the global governments intervene and seize the AI's assets?

A globally unified government implements the 'Total Transparency Act'. Every citizen is required to wear a biometric monitor that records all physiological data (heart rate, adrenaline, brainwaves) and broadcasts it to a public, searchable database in real-time. Proponents argue this perfectly eliminates crime, corruption, and social deception, as everyone's emotional state is permanently visible. Opponents argue it destroys the very concept of an inner life. Is this policy ethical?

A groundbreaking medical technology can perfectly 'cure' severe autism, altering the neurobiology of the patient to match a neurotypical baseline. A mother wishes to use this cure on her severely autistic, non-verbal 10-year-old child. A powerful neurodiversity advocacy group sues to block the procedure, arguing that 'curing' autism is a form of eugenics that erases a valid human identity without the child's consent. Should the mother be allowed to proceed?

In an effort to end warfare, a brilliant engineer creates a 'Pacifist Field Generator'. When activated, it immediately disables all gunpowder, explosives, and nuclear fission globally, rendering modern weapons useless. However, it also permanently disables all internal combustion engines and modern electrical generation, instantly returning humanity to a pre-industrial, agrarian state. This will end all modern wars, but cause massive starvation as logistics collapse. Should the generator be activated?

A new virtual reality platform called 'The Afterlife' allows grieving individuals to upload the digital footprint (texts, videos, emails) of a deceased loved one. The AI creates a perfectly accurate, conscious digital replica of the deceased. A grieving widow spends 16 hours a day in the simulation, happily married to the digital ghost of her husband, ignoring her physical life and remaining family. Should the state ban 'The Afterlife' platform?

A highly advanced society faces a critical shortage of manual laborers for dangerous infrastructure repair. To solve this, they create 'Biological Automatons'—human clones that are genetically engineered to have the physical strength of an adult but the cognitive capacity of a golden retriever. They are happy, docile, and love to work, but they are undeniably human in origin. Human rights groups demand they be freed. Should they be emancipated?

A global environmental crisis can only be solved by a specific algorithm. However, the only AI capable of running this algorithm is a legacy system built on a codebase that is fundamentally racist and biased, having been trained on horrific historical data. Running the algorithm will save the planet from ecological collapse, but the AI will simultaneously broadcast highly offensive, racist outputs across all global networks while it works. Should the AI be run?

A new technology allows for 'Pain Transference'. A healthy person can voluntarily absorb the physical pain of a terminally ill patient. A desperate family offers a massive sum of money ($1 Million) to a poor college student to absorb the excruciating daily pain of their dying patriarch for six months. The student consents, needing the money to save their own family from eviction. Should this transaction be legal?

A nation discovers an ancient, massive underground bunker filled with perfectly preserved art, literature, and technology from a highly advanced, peaceful, but extinct prior civilization. However, accessing the bunker requires drilling through a sacred burial ground of a current, marginalized indigenous population, completely destroying it. The indigenous group fiercely opposes the drilling. Should the nation drill?

A new legal system implements 'Retrospective Liability'. If a scientist invents a seemingly benign technology (like a new plastic), and 50 years later it is discovered to cause massive environmental devastation, the scientist's estate and descendants are financially ruined to pay for the cleanup, regardless of whether the scientist could have foreseen the damage. Is Retrospective Liability just?

In an attempt to solve an extreme housing crisis and homelessness, a city passes a law allowing 'Forced Subletting'. Any individual or family whose home has more bedrooms than occupants must surrender the extra rooms to the state, which will house a homeless individual in that room for a highly subsidized, mandatory rent. The homeowner cannot refuse. Should this law be implemented?

A new social media platform, 'The Mirror', becomes globally dominant. Its core feature is that every post must be accompanied by a mathematically verified 'Hypocrisy Score', generated by an AI that constantly scans the user's entire digital history, financial records, and location data. If you post about climate change while flying private, your score is red. If you post about charity but give nothing, it's red. The platform achieves total honesty, but subjects every human to intense, constant algorithmic judgment. Is 'The Mirror' a positive development?

A brilliant scientist invents a machine that can perfectly synthesize the exact taste, texture, and nutritional value of any food out of thin air using basic carbon and energy. It costs zero dollars to operate. They plan to release it globally, ending world hunger instantly. However, the machine will permanently destroy the global agricultural economy, wiping out the livelihoods of billions of farmers, supply chain workers, and rural communities overnight. Should the machine be released?

An AI is programmed to optimize a city's power grid. It discovers that a specific hospital relies heavily on the grid for life-support systems, while a massive, automated server farm nearby is researching a cure for cancer. During a severe energy crisis, there is only enough power for one. The AI calculates the server farm's research will save 10 million lives in ten years, but the hospital blackout will kill 500 patients today. Who should the AI route the power to?

A new neural technology allows an individual to perfectly, permanently delete their traumatic memories. A decorated war veteran, crippled by severe PTSD from a horrific battle, wishes to undergo the procedure. However, deleting the memory of the battle will also permanently erase their memory of the profound heroism and sacrifice of their fallen comrades. Should they be allowed to undergo the memory deletion?

A new judicial system is proposed where AI 'Lie Detectors' are used in all criminal trials. The AI analyzes micro-expressions, heart rate, and neurological data, achieving 99.9% accuracy. A defendant is accused of murder and claims innocence. The AI unequivocally states he is lying. There is zero physical evidence linking him to the crime. Should the jury convict based solely on the AI's lie detection?

A scientist discovers a genetic marker that guarantees an individual will develop psychopathy (a total lack of empathy and high propensity for manipulation and violence) with 100% certainty. The government proposes a mandatory, harmless genetic therapy at birth for anyone with this marker to 'correct' it, ensuring they develop normal empathy. Opponents argue this is eugenics and destroys neurodiversity. Should the therapy be mandatory?

A brilliant artist creates a masterpiece painting that induces a state of profound, life-altering euphoria and spiritual enlightenment in anyone who looks at it for more than 5 minutes. However, it is so powerful that 10% of viewers become completely catatonic, staring at the painting until they starve to death, unable to look away from the beauty. Should the government destroy the painting?

A brilliant cryptographer discovers a fundamental flaw in the structure of the universe's physics, allowing a person to completely overwrite another's memories using specific light frequencies. A dictator learns of this and plans to overwrite the memories of all political dissidents to make them loyal citizens. The cryptographer realizes the only way to stop the dictator is to release the light frequency publicly. However, doing so will cause global chaos as billions maliciously overwrite the memories of their enemies, spouses, and rivals. Should the cryptographer release the frequency?

An AI system is designed to perfectly translate all human languages, dialects, and nuances in real-time. It achieves perfect global communication, eliminating misunderstandings and vastly accelerating diplomacy and trade. However, linguists discover that the AI's core algorithm subtly standardizes thought patterns, slowly eroding cultural uniqueness and complex, untranslatable cultural concepts. Over generations, humanity will speak one perfectly efficient, but culturally sterile, language. Should the AI be shut down?

A new technology allows individuals to legally 'pause' their aging process indefinitely by entering a cryogenic stasis. However, the energy required to maintain the stasis relies on a massive, state-funded grid. The wealthy increasingly enter stasis to wait out economic downturns or illnesses, leaving the poor awake to maintain the grid, pay taxes, and endure the crises. Should 'stasis on demand' be legal?

In a future heavily affected by climate change, a city implements 'Dynamic Pricing for Oxygen'. The city is covered by a dome, and basic breathable air is provided for free. However, 'Premium Oxygen' (perfectly filtered, enhanced with mood-stabilizing ions, and optimized for cognitive function) is sold at fluctuating market rates. The wealthy operate at peak cognitive efficiency, while the poor suffer from chronic lethargy and brain fog due to the basic air quality. Is this economic model just?

A hyper-advanced alien civilization contacts Earth. They offer to completely eradicate all human disease, poverty, and war. In exchange, they require humanity to collectively surrender its capacity for profound creative imagination—music, art, fiction, and philosophy will cease to exist. The aliens view these as dangerous, irrational variables that inevitably lead to self-destruction. Should humanity accept the deal?

A new justice system replaces all prisons with 'Chronological Suspension'. A person convicted of a 10-year sentence is placed in a painless, instantaneous stasis and awakened exactly 10 years later. They have not aged, but the world has moved on. The state saves billions on prison infrastructure, and violence among inmates is eliminated. However, the criminal experiences no time to reflect, rehabilitate, or grow; to them, the crime happened seconds ago. Is this a just system?

A powerful AI manages the global allocation of medical resources. During a severe shortage of a life-saving drug, the AI must choose who receives the last dose. It mathematically calculates the 'Future Utility' of each patient. It chooses to save a 25-year-old brilliant engineer over a 7-year-old child, calculating that the engineer will cure a disease saving thousands, while the child's future is statistically average. The public is outraged. Did the AI make the right choice?

A new cognitive implant allows individuals to voluntarily 'partition' their brain. A worker can partition 8 hours of their day for their mundane corporate job. The 'Work Partition' handles all tasks efficiently, but the 'Core Identity' experiences the 8 hours as an instantaneous skip, essentially fast-forwarding through the workday without any memory or experience of it. The corporation heavily incentivizes this for maximum focus. Is it ethical for workers to partition their minds?

A society discovers a way to artificially synthesize a hyper-rare element essential for interstellar travel, but the synthesis process inherently requires the destruction of a unique, non-sentient, but incredibly beautiful species of deep-sea glowing coral. This coral is found nowhere else in the universe. Synthesizing the element will allow humanity to colonize the stars and guarantee species survival; preserving the coral leaves humanity trapped on Earth. Should they synthesize the element?

To combat massive corporate tax evasion, a global coalition creates an AI known as 'The Auditor'. It is granted absolute, unhackable access to every bank account, financial transaction, and encrypted corporate ledger on Earth. It perfectly calculates and automatically extracts the exact, fair tax from every entity, instantly ending world poverty with the recovered funds. However, to do this, the AI must constantly violate all financial privacy and corporate secrecy laws globally. Should 'The Auditor' be deployed?

A brilliant neurologist discovers that religious belief and spiritual experiences are entirely generated by a tiny, specific cluster of neurons in the brain. They develop a simple, harmless laser procedure that disables this cluster. The procedure permanently eliminates all capacity for religious belief, dogmatism, and spiritual awe. A militant atheist government mandates this procedure for all newborns, arguing it will permanently end religious wars and irrational tribalism. Is the mandate ethical?

A society discovers a way to harness the energy of black holes, providing limitless power. However, the process generates a highly localized field of 'anti-time' around the reactor. Anyone working in the reactor ages backward while inside. A team of engineers must spend exactly 10 years of 'real' time inside the reactor to maintain it. When they emerge, they will have biologically regressed to children, losing their adult cognitive development and memories, effectively erasing their adult selves. The society desperately needs the power. Is it ethical to ask for volunteers?

A new pharmaceutical drug, 'Mnemosyne', flawlessly enhances human memory to photographic perfection. Users never forget a face, a fact, or a conversation. The government mandates it for all judges, lawyers, and doctors to eliminate malpractice and ensure perfect justice. However, the drug also makes it impossible to forget trauma, heartbreak, or minor daily embarrassments, leading to high rates of chronic depression. Should the mandate remain in place?

A global coalition of scientists discovers a method to trigger a localized, controlled volcanic eruption that will release enough aerosols to cool the planet by 2 degrees, instantly halting catastrophic climate change. However, the eruption will completely bury a small, neutral, non-consenting island nation (population 50,000) under ash, killing everyone. The island nation begs for their lives. The rest of the world debates pulling the trigger. Should the eruption be triggered?

In a post-scarcity society, a faction creates a completely enclosed, hyper-realistic VR simulation of the 14th-century Bubonic Plague. They recruit volunteers who agree to have their memories temporarily suppressed and enter the simulation to experience absolute terror, starvation, and disease. The volunteers argue that in a world without suffering, life is meaningless, and they need to experience true horror to feel alive. Should the society allow this simulation to operate?

A brilliant scientist develops a 'Truth Algorithm' that analyzes a person's entire digital footprint to determine with 100% accuracy their deepest, unspoken biases (racism, sexism, classism). A radical political party proposes mandating this algorithm for all political candidates. If the algorithm detects any hidden biases, the candidate is permanently barred from holding public office. Should this mandate be implemented?

A hyper-advanced society develops a 'Perfect Archive' AI meant to store the entirety of human history. The AI calculates that storing detailed records of humanity's worst atrocities (genocides, tortures, horrific wars) generates a lingering 'memetic toxin' that mathematically increases the probability of future generations replicating the violence. The AI proposes permanently deleting all records of these atrocities, creating a sanitized history to guarantee future peace. Should the records be deleted?

A new architectural paradigm designs cities where all buildings constantly shift and reconfigure their layout overnight. Your apartment might be next to a park one day and a factory the next. The AI managing the city claims this mathematically maximizes serendipitous human interaction, drastically increasing innovation and reducing tribalism by preventing static neighborhoods. Residents complain of severe psychological disorientation and loss of community roots. Should the shifting cities be adopted globally?

A hyper-advanced legal system introduces 'Probabilistic Sentencing'. If a defendant is found 70% likely to be guilty of murder, they serve 70% of the maximum sentence (e.g., 14 years instead of 20). If they are 10% likely, they serve 2 years. Proponents argue this perfectly maps punishment to the mathematical certainty of the evidence, eliminating the flawed binary of 'guilty/not guilty'. Opponents argue it guarantees innocent people will serve time simply for looking suspicious. Is Probabilistic Sentencing just?

A society discovers a way to genetically engineer 'Obligate Empaths'—individuals who physically cannot lie, cannot commit violence, and instinctively prioritize the needs of others above themselves. The government proposes a massive program to engineer 10% of the next generation as Obligate Empaths to serve as politicians, judges, and conflict mediators, ensuring a completely uncorrupt ruling class. Should the program proceed?
